source.title: Spatial representations of self and other in the hippocampus

confidence_rationale: An independent convergent replication of the Omer result in a different species (rat), different paradigm (observational T-maze) and different laboratory, published back-to-back. The convergence raises confidence that other-agent spatial coding in the hippocampus is real rather than paradigm-specific. Direction is mixed for the same reason as Omer: the authors report self and other are 'jointly and discretely encoded' (supports separability) while a subset of CA1 cells had spatial receptive fields IDENTICAL for self and other (weakens token-keying). Held at 0.60, matching Omer, since the mapping limitation is identical.
failure_signatures: A subset of CA1 pyramidal cells had spatial receptive fields that were identical for self and for the other animal -- these cells cannot be said to key a representation to a particular agent token at all, since the same cell fires for the same place regardless of who occupies it.

As with Omer et al., only the spatial field of ARC-083's proposed slot is evidenced; the paradigm cannot speak to whether a persistent per-agent file survives the other animal leaving the maze, which is the 'permanence' half of the claim's stated prerequisite.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Recording CA1 pyramidal cells in rats performing an observational T-maze task, the authors found that information reflecting the spatial location of both the self and the other was jointly and discretely encoded. A subset of CA1 pyramidal cells exhibited spatial receptive fields that were identical for the self and the other.
mapping.ree_translation: Converges with Omer et al. (2018) in supporting ARC-083's premise that another agent's state is carried inside the ordinary spatial/object representational machinery rather than in a dedicated social module. 'Jointly and discretely encoded' is the phrase that does the most work for REE: it asserts that self and other are simultaneously present AND distinguishable within one population -- which is closer to a multiplexed field than to the discrete per-agent slot ARC-083 specifies, but is at least a code from which distinct agent identities are recoverable.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Rat CA1 during a constrained two-arm observational task with a single other animal. A single-other paradigm cannot test the property that makes ARC-083's claim architectural -- that each of SEVERAL others gets its own token-keyed slot. Distinguishing self from one other is a far weaker result than maintaining separate persistent files for agents j=1..n, and the transfer to the latter is an extrapolation this paper does not license.
mapping.source_context: Rat; dorsal CA1 single-unit recording; observational T-maze task with one conspecific.

confidence_components.notes: Science, back-to-back with Omer, independent lab and species -- the convergence is the main source-quality asset. Mapping capped by the single-other paradigm, which cannot address the multi-agent slot allocation that is ARC-083's actual content.
